lead:
Plateau ordered every public and private primary and secondary school to close from Monday as suspected diphtheria cases spread to four local government areas.

The day in brief: the closure came days after health officials confirmed deaths in Jos North from suspected diphtheria complications. The Auditor-General's 2024 report said the government could not show that N33.75 billion paid to more than 3.29 million households in 2023 reached genuine beneficiaries, and Atiku Abubakar called it an indictment. The SEC approved the Dangote refinery's IPO of 4.1 billion shares at N525 each, which could raise about N2.15 trillion, opening on 14 September. The House of Representatives dissolved all its ad hoc committees, the APC in Kano received two former senators and 136,038 other defectors at a rally after which journalists were attacked, and the Civil Defence Corps said it rescued 15 children sold for N2 million each. Fires destroyed shops in Kano and Ilorin, the First Niger Bridge was set to close for two weeks of repairs, and D'Tigress opened their World Cup with a defeat by South Korea.

items.h: Plateau shuts all schools over diphtheria
items.s: Information Commissioner Joyce Ramnap announced on Saturday that all public and private primary and secondary schools in Plateau would close temporarily from Monday, 7 September, until further notice, after suspected diphtheria cases appeared in four local government areas. The government said the step was meant to protect pupils, days after officials confirmed deaths in Jos North.

items.h: Auditor-General flags N33.75bn in cash transfers without proof of recipients
items.s: The Auditor-General's 2024 report on non-compliance and internal control weaknesses said the government could not provide sufficient evidence that N33.75 billion in electronic cash transfers to more than 3.29 million vulnerable households in 2023 reached genuine beneficiaries. Atiku Abubakar called the finding an indictment of the administration.

items.h: Dangote refinery share sale reported to open on 14 September
items.s: The SEC approved the Dangote refinery's IPO of 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 each, which could raise about N2.15 trillion if fully subscribed, Dangote Group said, in what is expected to be Africa's biggest share sale. The offer was reported to open on 14 September.

items.h: JAMB releases underage candidates' UTME results
items.s: JAMB released the 2026 UTME results of underage candidates for viewing, but its spokesman Fabian Benjamin said this does not make them all eligible for admission; only exceptionally high scorers will be considered.

items.h: House of Representatives dissolves all ad hoc committees
items.s: The Clerk of the House of Representatives, Sidi Ibrahim, said all ad hoc committees were dissolved with immediate effect on the directive of Speaker Abbas Tajudeen, after the time given to them to finish their assignments and submit reports expired.

items.h: NSCDC rescues 15 children allegedly sold for N2m each
items.s: NSCDC spokesman Babawale Afolabi said the Commandant-General's special squad rescued 15 children allegedly sold for N2 million each in Nasarawa by a man posing as an official of a child rights group to deceive parents, and arrested two suspects. The squad also recovered stolen rifles and broke up a telecom vandalism ring.

items.h: Wike says Amaechi neglected Rivers as transport minister
items.s: At a civic reception in Omagwa, Ikwerre, FCT Minister Nyesom Wike accused Rotimi Amaechi, now the ADC's vice-presidential candidate, of neglecting Rivers State while he was transport minister, said he had lost political credibility, and declared that Rivers voters would back President Tinubu.

items.h: Former senators and 136,038 others join APC in Kano; journalists attacked
items.s: At the Sani Abacha Stadium in Kano, the APC received former senators Rufa'i Hanga and Kabiru Gaya, NNPP faction chairman Mas'ud Doguwa and 136,038 other defectors as it unveiled Tinubu campaign groups. Suspected thugs attacked journalists returning from the rally.

items.h: Makinde says Nigerians should not pay for government's failures on fuel
items.s: In his newsletter, Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde said Nigerians should not pay extra because the government cannot secure its borders, and that the fuel debate has been wrongly reduced to removing or restoring subsidy. He called for transparency on how pump prices are set, including the crude benchmark, refining costs and exchange rates.

items.h: APM to open Makinde's presidential campaign office in Abuja
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement said its candidate, Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde, would commission the Makinde/Daura presidential campaign office in Abuja on Monday, to serve as the national hub of a campaign it said would be issue-based.

items.h: APM says Tinubu lacks capacity to tackle insecurity
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement accused the government of downplaying insecurity, saying Nigeria now ranks as the fourth most terrorism-affected country in the 2026 Global Terrorism Index, and criticised Defence Minister Christopher Musa for what it called a dangerous distortion of the facts.

items.h: Former IGP Mohammed Adamu becomes Nasarawa SDP governorship candidate
items.s: The SDP declared former Inspector-General Mohammed Abubakar Adamu its Nasarawa governorship candidate after a replacement primary across the state's 13 local governments at the Ta'al Hotel in Lafia, held to replace candidates who withdrew, committee chairman Joseph Achille said.

items.h: First Niger Bridge to close from 7 to 21 September
items.s: The First Niger Bridge was to close to traffic from 7 to 21 September for emergency maintenance and rehabilitation by the Federal Ministry of Works, the Anambra government and acting federal controller of works Timothy Emenike said, asking motorists to take note.

items.h: Fire destroys shops and six houses at Kano's Kofar Wambai market
items.s: Fire that started at about 9.43pm on Friday on the upper floor of a building in the Babban Layi, Yan Robobi plastics section of Kofar Wambai Market, Kano, destroyed shops, stores and six houses, fire service spokesman Saminu Abdullahi said.

items.h: Midnight fire destroys 12 shops in Ilorin
items.s: Goods worth millions of naira were destroyed when fire swept through 12 of about 40 shops in a complex near Mandate Market, opposite Alkad Filling Station in Ilorin, shortly after midnight on Saturday, eyewitnesses said.

items.h: Lagos police arrest suspected kidnappers after N21m ransom
items.s: Lagos anti-kidnapping officers arrested Semi Buawe, 35, Bamure Telemowei and Oluwatomi Obosi, 37, suspected members of a gang based in Agadagba, Ese-Odo, Ondo State, that travelled to abduct Lagos residents, after a N21 million ransom was paid for one victim.

items.h: Two dead after youth clash in Dass, Bauchi
items.s: Two people were killed in attacks that followed a clash between youths in Dass, Bauchi, on 4 September, after a 29-year-old tricycle rider, Abdulrahman Nuru, was allegedly intercepted and attacked at Tudun Wus. Police arrested seven suspects.

items.h: Anambra police arrest suspect 82 days after nursing student's murder
items.s: Anambra police arrested Kosisochukwu Edward Ibekwe, 26, on 4 September over the murder of nursing student Vivian Chilaka, 23, in Alor, Idemili South, on 14 June, 82 days after her death.

items.h: Troops kill terrorist and seize motorcycles in Katsina forest
items.s: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma killed a terrorist and recovered four motorcycles in a dawn raid on a suspected terrorist health facility in Dan Musa, Katsina, on Friday, 4 September, the task force's media officer said.

items.h: Katsina police arrest 247 and rescue 17 kidnap victims in August
items.s: Katsina police said they arrested 247 suspects and rescued 17 kidnap victims in August, spokesman Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu said for Commissioner Ali Umar Fage at a press conference in Katsina.

items.h: Army trains first cohort of Borno forest guards
items.s: The first cohort of Borno State Forest Guards passed out on 5 September after six weeks of army training in combat support and law enforcement at the Miangu Range, Rukuba Barracks, Jos, strengthening the state's community-based security.

items.h: Police warn politicians that incitement is a crime
items.s: Force spokesman Anietie Iniedu warned politicians that incitement is a criminal offence under Nigerian law and that the police will not tolerate remarks that could trigger electoral violence before the 2027 elections.

items.h: Delta police arrest six, including a 15-year-old, over drug sales
items.s: Delta police arrested six suspected drug dealers, including a 15-year-old girl, as part of a crackdown on the sale and distribution of illicit drugs, spokesman Bright Edafe said.

items.h: Police rescue woman kidnapped in Sapele
items.s: Delta police rescued a woman whom gunmen ambushed at the entrance of her home in Sapele and took into the bush, after the Sapele division received a distress call, spokesman Bright Edafe said.

items.h: World Bank safety-net payments to Nigeria reach $744m
items.s: Nigeria drew a further $208.29 million under the World Bank's $800 million National Social Safety Net Programme scale-up, bringing disbursements to about $744.61 million, as the government relies on cash transfers to support poor households.

items.h: Uba Sani unveils locally assembled Peugeot 5008
items.s: Kaduna Governor Uba Sani unveiled the 2026 Peugeot 5008 at the Dangote Peugeot Automobile Nigeria plant and said he will ask the National Economic Council to urge ministries and agencies to buy locally assembled vehicles to protect jobs and support manufacturing.

items.h: IMSU lecturers say they will not grade exams held during strike
items.s: ASUU's Imo State University branch chairman, Stephen Oguji, said lecturers will not mark scripts from examinations held while the union's strike continues, and warned students sitting such exams.

items.h: Uba Sani gives plots and cash to 255 APC ward chairmen
items.s: Kaduna Governor Uba Sani gave a plot of land and cash to each of the APC's 255 ward chairmen in the state, the head of the land agency KADGIS, Bashir Garba Ibrahim, said for him at a capacity workshop for party officials.

items.h: Barau unveils Kano North campaign council
items.s: Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin unveiled the APC campaign council for Kano North, with Rabiu Sulaiman Bichi among its leaders, and directed party officials to begin house-to-house mobilisation for the 16 January 2027 elections.

items.h: Oyo APC presents its 2027 candidates
items.s: The Oyo APC presented its 2027 candidates at its Oke Ado secretariat in Ibadan, giving certificates to governorship candidate Senator Sharafadeen Alli, who asked members to treat his former rivals as brothers whose support he needs.

items.h: Taraba governor picks Zainab Ibrahim as running mate
items.s: Taraba Governor Agbu Kefas named Hajiya Zainab Ibrahim as his running mate for 2027, in place of his deputy Aminu Alkali, who has been with him since 2023 but is reported to be in poor health.

items.h: NDC aspirant sues party and INEC over Delta governorship primary
items.s: Ejaife Omizu Odebala filed a suit at the Federal High Court in Abuja against the NDC, INEC and four others, asking to be declared winner of the party's Delta governorship primary.

items.h: Osinbajo warns about unsafe fresh orange juice
items.s: Former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo told a gardeners' seminar in Lagos that laboratory tests found freshly squeezed orange juice his wife Dolapo regularly drank was unfit for consumption, after she developed unusual headaches.

items.h: D'Tigress face Hungary after opening loss
items.s: Nigeria's women started their FIBA World Cup in Berlin with a 99-81 loss to South Korea in Group B, despite racing to a 6-0 lead and staying close for long spells. Coach Rena Wakama's African champions turned their attention to Hungary next.

items.h: Osimhen doubtful for AFCON qualifiers
items.s: Victor Osimhen became a doubt for Nigeria's AFCON qualifiers after being forced off in the 33rd minute of Galatasaray's 3-2 win at Istanbul Basaksehir, having scored in the 16th minute.

items.h: US destroys three Iranian oil tankers
items.s: The US military said it destroyed three Iranian oil tankers after alleged failed missile attacks on US naval vessels, escalating the six-month conflict in which Iran holds the Strait of Hormuz and Washington is trying to blockade Iranian ports.
